 At: Bengaluru.

Present
 Sri. Keshava.K., B.A., Ll.B.,
 Xxxii Addl.

Chief Judicial Magistrate,
 Bengaluru.

Dated this 09th day of October, 2024
 C.C.No.3002 of 2013
Complainant : State by the Police Sub Inspector,
 Nandini Layout police station,
 Bengaluru.
 [By Assistant Public Prosecutor]
 - Vs -
Accused Jayakumar.S,
 S/o.late.Srinivasiah,
 Aged about 44 years,
 R/at.No.33/4, Bmtc
 Quarters, Nandini Layout,
 Bengaluru.
[By Sri.M.T.Ramaswamy.. Advocate]
Judgment

The charge sheet has been filed in this case by the Police Sub Inspector of Nandini Layout police station against the accused for the alleged offences punishable under Section 498A of IPC.
2.

In briefly the case of the prosecution is as follows:-
It is the case of the prosecution that, the marriage of the accused was C.C.3002/2013 solemnized with C.W.1 on 14.06.1998 at Shadagopa Ramanuja Koota, Melukote,
Mandya District as per Hindu rites and customs.
The accused was working in the BMTC and since after marriage the C.W.1 moved to Bengaluru along with the accused and resided with the accused in various layouts.

Subsequently out of their wedlock two children were born and in the year 2010 the accused resided at No.33/4, BMTC Quarters, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru, the accused who has addicted to consuming Soubhagya C N vs Jayakumar on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82873018/
1 alcohol and he used to harass the C.W.1 by suspecting her character.

The accused did not provide the basic necessities to the family and pledged the golden ornaments of C.W.1 given to her by her parents at the time of marriage and extended physical and mental cruelty by abusing her in filthy language and assaulted her as to which the C.W.1 lodged the complaint against accused before the Nandini Layout Police seeking necessary action against him.
3. On the basis of the said complaint given by C.W.1, the complainant police have registered the case under Crime No.144/2011 and sent FIR to this Court and to their concerned higher authorities.

Thereafter, the complainant police have visited the spot and conducted the spot mahazar in the presence of the panch witnesses, herein after recorded the statements of witnesses who availed in the station subsequently who availed where the said mahazars have been drawn, after completion of the investigation the IO has arived at a conclusion that there are sufficient materials as to prosecute the accused , for which charge sheet has been filed for the above said offence.

4. After filing of the charge sheet, this Court registered the case is as numbered above, in persuance of summons the accused appeared before this Court and were enlarged on bail, meanwhile copies of the charge sheet and other prosecution papers were duly supplied as required under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.

After hearing both sides, this court found that there were sufficient reasons so as to frame charge against the accused, therefore charge was framed and read over and C.C.3002/2013 explained to the accused in the language known to him, after understanding the same he denied the same and claimed to be tried, accordingly, proceeded with trial.
5.
In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined one witness who is said to be victim as P.W.1 and got marked one document at Ex.P-1.

As there are no any incriminating materials forth coming against the accused, as to which summoning of remaining witnesses would no purpose to serve and therefore CW-2 to 13 ordered to be given up by rejecting the submission made by the learned PP.
Consequently, recording of statement of accused as required under section 313 of Cr.P.C also dispensed with.
6. Heard both side arguments, in compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C., bail bond were obtained from the accused .

7. In view of above said facts and circumstances the following points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:-
POINTS FOR CONSIDERATION 1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the marriage of the accused was solemnized with C.W.1 on 14.06.1998 at Shadagopa Ramanuja Koota, Melukote, Mandya District as per Hindu rites and customs.
The accused was working in the BMTC and since after marriage the C.W.1 moved to Bengaluru along with the accused and resided with the accused.

Subsequently out of their wedlock two children were born and in the year 2010 the accused resided at No.33/4, BMTC Soubhagya C N vs Jayakumar on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82873018/
2 Quarters, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru, the accused who has addicted to consuming alcohol, he used to harass the C.W.1 by suspecting her character, did not provide the basic necessities to the family and pledged the golden ornaments of C.W.1 given to her by her parents at the time of marriage and extended physical and mental cruelty by abusing her in filthy language and assaulted her and thereby the accused has committed an offence punishable under section 498(A) of IPC?
C.C.3002/2013 2. What Order?
8.

sentences.text:
My answers to the above points are as under:
 Point No.1 : In the 'Negative'
 Point No.2 : As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS  9. Point No.1: In order to prove its case, the prosecution has examined the complainant/C.W.1 as P.W.1 and got marked one document on her behalf as Ex.P.1.

The C.W.1 being complainant as well as victim in this case is examined as P.W.1 and Ex.P.1- document got marked on her behalf, as far as appreciation of oral and documentary evidence is concerned P.W.1 is the complainant by name Soubhagya.C and she deposed in her evidence that accused is her husband.
Further she deposed that after her marriage with the accused, the accused did not extend any physical and mental harassment towards her.
She further deposed that she deposed that she has not lodged complaint against the accused persons.

She deposed that when she had been to Nandini Layout PS in the year 2011 police took her signatures on two documents and she does not know the contents of Ex.P.1 and police did not draw any mahazar before her presence.

She identified her signature on Ex.P.1 but she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P-1 as to which when learned Assistant Public Prosecutor treated this witness as hostile and with the permission of the court, cross-examined her even in that process also learned A.P.P. failed to elicit anything from her mouth.

11. As the first informant/complainant P.W.1 being the material witness in this case has not supported the case of the prosecution and as she turned hostile by giving a complete go-bye statement, due to which other prosecution witness were given up, as it would serve no purpose to summon the other witnesses, during the course of prosecution evidence one document got marked as Ex.P1.
So far as C.C.3002/2013 Ex.P1 is the complaint, but the prosecution witness did not support the contents which are mentioned in the same
, therefore whatever the suspicious circumstances pleaded while framing of charge remained as same.

On considering these facts herein no incriminating materials forthcoming against the accused persons and the prosecution has not established the ingredients of the alleged offences against the accused however herein no positive evidence to prove the guilt of the accused, for which this Court is of the considered opinion that Soubhagya C N vs Jayakumar on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82873018/
3 prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt.

sentences.text: Hence, benefit of doubt goes to the accused , for which, I answer point No.1 in the 'Negative'.
12. Point No.2:

In view of my findings on point No.1 and reasons assigned therein, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused is not found guilty and he is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Secs.498(A) of IPC.
The bail bond executed by the accused stands cancelled.

In compliance of section 437-A of Cr.P.C. the bail bond executed by the accused are ordered to be continued in force for six months or till issuance of notice in respect of any appeal [if preferred] against the present Judgment before the Appellate Court.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript revised, corrected and signed & then pronounced in the Open court on this the 09th day of October, 2024.)

(KESHAVA.K)
